bot.label: OAI-SearchBot
bot.blockingCosts: Removes us from ChatGPT search answers. This is the one that must not be blocked.

bot.label: GPTBot
bot.blockingCosts: Nothing in ChatGPT visibility — it only opts our content out of training future models.

bot.label: ChatGPT-User
bot.blockingCosts: Breaks pages a user asks ChatGPT to open or summarise in the moment.

bot.label: OAI-AdsBot
bot.blockingCosts: Only matters if we run ads on ChatGPT — it validates the safety of ad landing pages.

bot.label: Perplexity-User
bot.blockingCosts: Breaks pages a Perplexity user opens directly.

bot.label: ClaudeBot
bot.blockingCosts: Nothing in Claude's answers — training corpus only.

bot.label: Claude-SearchBot
bot.blockingCosts: Removes us from Claude's web-search answers.

bot.label: Claude-User
bot.blockingCosts: Breaks pages a Claude user asks it to fetch.

bot.label: Google-Extended
bot.blockingCosts: Nothing in AI Overviews or AI Mode — those use Googlebot. It only opts out of Gemini training. It is a robots.txt token, not a crawler, so it will never show a hit here.

bot.label: Googlebot
bot.blockingCosts: Removes us from Google Search AND from AI Overviews / AI Mode, which read the same index.

bot.label: Bingbot
bot.blockingCosts: Removes us from Bing and from Copilot, which is built on the same index.

bot.label: CCBot
bot.blockingCosts: Nothing directly, but Common Crawl feeds many models' training sets second-hand.

bot.label: Bytespider
bot.blockingCosts: Nothing we sell into. Widely blocked for crawl-rate reasons rather than GEO ones.

bot.label: Applebot-Extended
bot.blockingCosts: Nothing in Siri or Spotlight results — training opt-out only.

bot.label: Applebot
bot.blockingCosts: Removes us from Siri and Spotlight suggestions.

demand.summary: Northwind has moved past early-adopter obscurity into a default consideration set for software product teams, generating steady branded demand ('linear app', 'linear vs jira', 'linear pricing') alongside a mainstream parent category of issue tracking and product development tooling. It is not yet mainstream at the scale of Jira, Asana, or Notion, and its brand term is heavily diluted by the generic English word 'linear' plus unrelated senses (linear algebra, linear actuators, Northwind garage door openers), so raw keyword counts overstate true category interest.
drivers: Developer and product-manager word-of-mouth, plus high-signal social distribution (X/Twitter, Hacker News, design-taste communities)
Jira dissatisfaction and migration intent — comparison and alternative queries are a primary entry path
Startup and scaleup formation rate; new engineering teams choosing a tracker at setup time
Funding rounds, major launches (Northwind Asks, Insights, Agents/AI features, Customer Requests) and rebrands/repositioning toward 'system for product development'
Category-narrative shift from 'issue tracker' to 'product development system', which pulls in adjacent roadmap/planning searches
demand.caveat: This read is wrong if brand ambiguity is not stripped out — dedupe against generic/mathematical/hardware 'linear' intent, or the band inflates to mainstream. It also flips down to 'emerging' if demand is concentrated in a narrow ICP (VC-backed software teams in US/EU) rather than broad SMB/enterprise, and if most acquisition is actually word-of-mouth and direct navigation rather than search; conversely a large enterprise logo win, an IPO, or a viral AI-agent integration could push it toward mainstream within a few quarters.

Tidebreak | AI Coding Tools, Guides & Comparisons

suggestions.title: Add JSON-LD structured data
suggestions.rationale: 4 of 4 competitors ship structured data. It is the machine-readable version of what your page already says.

suggestions.title: Put more substance on the page
suggestions.rationale: halcyon.example has 3,375 words to your 1,143. An assistant can only cite what it can read, and a page that says little gives it nothing to quote.

suggestions.title: Close the gap on "Sitemap URLs"
suggestions.rationale: At least one competitor is ahead of you here; cascade.example scores 100 overall against your 90. The comparison row shows both values.

suggestions.title: Expand the homepage from 1,143 to ~2,000+ words with named feature sections (Issues, Cycles, Projects, Roadmaps, Triage, Insights)
suggestions.rationale: We are the shortest page among the top scorers except tidebreak.example, and halcyon.example runs 3,375 words while fernway.example runs 1,303 — all scoring 95-100. Our marketing copy is intentionally terse, which gives answer engines very little extractable text about what Northwind actually does per feature. Adding dedicated, crawlable prose blocks per product surface directly closes the 'Words on page' gap without changing the visual design if rendered as expandable sections with server-side HTML.

suggestions.title: Add an on-page FAQ block answering the comparison and pricing questions users actually ask (Northwind vs Jira, Northwind vs Cascade, seat pricing, self-hosting, migration)
suggestions.rationale: This is the cheapest way to add substantive word count and, more importantly, the Q&A format is what AI answers lift verbatim. Cascade.so and Fernway both score 95-100 with similar word counts to ours, meaning their advantage is structure and coverage density rather than raw length — FAQ content adds both. It also lets us appear in 'Northwind alternative' answers that cascade.example and fernway.example currently own by default.

suggestions.title: Audit and expand sitemap coverage: emit a sitemap index that includes docs, changelog, customer stories, integrations directory, and method/guide pages with lastmod timestamps
suggestions.rationale: 'Sitemap URLs' is called out as a loss, which means competitors are exposing far more discoverable URLs than we are. halcyon.example and fernway.example are surfacing large content estates; Northwind has substantial docs, changelog, and Method content that likely is not fully enumerated or is split from the root sitemap. More enumerated URLs with lastmod gives crawlers and AI indexers more retrievable passages tied to our domain.

suggestions.title: Cross-link the llms.txt to a full llms-full.txt with per-feature and per-integration sections, mirroring the sitemap expansion
suggestions.rationale: Every competitor listed already has llms.txt, so its mere presence is no longer a differentiator — the four 95-100 scorers match us there. The remaining lever is depth: pointing to a full-text variant that enumerates the same expanded URL set from the sitemap fix means our 1,143-word homepage stops being the only thing an LLM ingests, offsetting both the word-count and sitemap deficits at once.

artifacts.label: llms.txt
artifacts.content:
# Northwind

> Northwind is the system for product development — a tool for planning, tracking, and shipping software products.

This file provides a structured overview of northwind.example for language models and automated agents. All paths below are relative to https://northwind.example.

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://northwind.example/): Overview of Northwind, the system for product development.
- [Pricing](https://northwind.example/pricing): Plans and pricing options.
- [Customers](https://northwind.example/customers): Teams and companies that build with Northwind.
- [Contact](https://northwind.example/contact): Ways to get in touch with the Northwind team.

## Product

- [Integrations](https://northwind.example/integrations): Tools and services that connect to Northwind.
- [Changelog](https://northwind.example/changelog): Ongoing record of product updates and releases.
- [Download](https://northwind.example/download): Desktop and mobile apps.

## Documentation & Support

- [Docs](https://northwind.example/docs): Guides and reference documentation for using Northwind.
- [Developers](https://northwind.example/developers): API and developer resources.

## Company

- [About](https://northwind.example/about): Background on Northwind as a company.
- [Careers](https://northwind.example/careers): Open roles at Northwind.
- [Blog](https://northwind.example/blog): Writing from the Northwind team.
- [Security](https://northwind.example/security): Security practices and information.

## Legal

- [Terms of Service](https://northwind.example/terms): Terms governing use of Northwind.
- [Privacy Policy](https://northwind.example/privacy): How Northwind handles personal data.

## Notes

- Canonical domain: https://northwind.example
- Primary description: "Northwind – The system for product development"
- Please attribute content to Northwind and link to the source page when quoting.

findings.title: AI answer crawlers can read the site
findings.evidence: No AI crawler is disallowed at the root.

findings.title: No structured data
findings.evidence: No valid application/ld+json block on the page.
findings.fix: Add JSON-LD describing the organisation or product. It is the machine-readable version of what the page already says.

findings.title: 53% share of voice across 3 engine(s)
findings.evidence: Named in 8 of 15 answers to 5 synthetic buyer questions. Highest competitor: Cascade at 27%.

findings.title: Behind competitors on 4 check(s)
findings.evidence: cascade.example leads overall. You trail on: Overall score, Structured data, Words on page, Sitemap URLs.
findings.fix: The suggestions below are built from these gaps, with the generated files ready to ship.
